title: Arkret Service Describe
description: Canonical role-scoped ServiceDescribe response. Runtime operation availability is the union of registered supported_operation_bundles intersected with usable transport_bindings; supported_features is the sole feature claim set. Profile claims remain conformance evidence and never add operations. Exact source-tree, generated-registry, SDK, service-build, or release-artifact fingerprints are not compatibility carriers and MUST remain outside this document and all protocol decisions.

service_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the service making this describe claim. It cannot be resolved without service_resolution or another verified AuthenticatedServiceResolution.

service_resolution.description: Read-only current did commitment for this service role. Describe is a second-hop endpoint confirmation surface, not a did_core_id resolver: callers already need a candidate URL before fetching it and MUST verify the did projection, method evidence and endpoint reverse binding before updating a route cache.

trust_domain.description: Deployment-scope trust domain for this service. Receivers use it as the canonical receive-context replay boundary for cross-deployment proofs and federation transactions.

service_kind.description: One logical role this service plays on the wire. Each ServiceDescribe document describes exactly one role; co-located roles sharing a public binding use separate role-scoped responses selected by GET /_arkret/describe?service_kind=<registered-id>. The value space is registry/service-kind-registry.json filtered to active rows whose valid_in contains service_describe.

protocol_version.description: Arkret protocol-family bootstrap discriminator. A consumer first extracts this field before applying the version-specific ServiceDescribe schema: a well-formed value other than 1.0 yields unsupported_protocol_version, while missing or non-string values yield schema_violation. The const keeps an object admitted as ak.schema.service_describe.v1 closed to Arkret/1.

supported_profiles.description: The sole complete-profile self-declaration for this exact build and role endpoint. Every declared profile MUST satisfy its full applicable contract. Feature-only support belongs in supported_features. verified_profiles supplies independent evidence, never an alternate activation set; each verified profile MUST also occur here.

supported_reducer_profiles.description: Registered Realm reducer profiles this service can execute. This is a runtime capability set, not a conformance claim and not a selected Realm profile.

profile_bindings.description: Profile-specific carrier declarations keyed by profile id. A profile that mandates one interoperable private carrier must bind it here rather than relying on a product-local route.

supported_features.description: Canonical-sorted exact registered feature ids this role endpoint currently supports. This is the sole public runtime feature claim set.

calendar_tzdb_versions.description: IANA TZDB release tags this service can execute for calendar schedules, taken from calendar-timezone-registry.json. Required when the service claims a calendar profile. A schedule whose signed tzdb_version is absent here MUST fail closed with calendar_tzdb_mismatch or project its instants as unresolved; the service MUST NOT fall back to a nearby or newer release.

auth_metadata.description: Authentication and session metadata needed by clients before calling protected operations. Unregistered keys are limited to safely ignorable x_* metadata.

methods.description: Authentication methods offered for this principal/account surface. Methods describe proof providers, standard discovery, and the proof kind accepted by the Account Authority. Arkret gate/account routing is always derived from account_authority.

did_binding_methods.description: session_dpop is the mandatory default SessionGrant presentation; session_http_signature is only an additional high-security body/transcript binding layer. did_http_signature denotes separately registered DID proofs and is never a SessionGrant fallback.

limits.description: Operational limits such as body size, batch size, TTL, pagination or retention bounds.

plaintext_visibility.description: Plaintext boundary declaration. Omission is not allowed: callers use this object to decide whether the service may be registered as plaintext-visible. An empty object means the service claims no plaintext classes; Realm plaintext_visible_services entries MUST match non-empty data_classes here.

data_classes.description: Closed machine-checkable classes of plaintext or reversible derived content this service is implemented to receive.

max_visibility.description: Maximum plaintext visibility class the service claims it can receive. Omitted is treated as none unless data_classes is non-empty.

privacy_derivation.description: Machine-readable privacy-preserving identifier derivation claims. Secret material is never published here; only profile and epoch metadata needed for audit and rotation checks.

secret_scope.description: The HMAC salt/pepper is unique to this service context and MUST NOT be shared across Stations, organizations, or push routes.

salt_epoch_id.description: Opaque public epoch label for the active secret. This is not the secret salt value.

receive_policy_constraints.description: Deployment/admin upper bound for subject-private invite/contact receive policies. Stations SHOULD expose this in describe so clients can show which user reachability preferences are capped by server policy.

rate_limit_policy_id.description: Identifier for a cacheable, verifiable rate-limit policy object with the same minimum fields as rate_limit_policy. See zh/sync/api-conventions.md §8.

rate_limit_policy.description: Inline rate-limit policy. If the service can return rate_limited, entries[] MUST expose at least endpoint or operation_id, rate_limit_scope, a window/limit tuple or a retry hint; an empty entries[] explicitly means no predictable endpoint-level rate limit beyond generic abuse protection.

endpoint.description: Closed endpoint selector: either an absolute HTTP(S) URL or an absolute-path endpoint on this service.

egress_network_policy.description: Coarse outbound-network policy for SSRF protection. Public describe MAY omit sensitive allowlist entries; authenticated operator describe MAY return the complete policy. Normative semantics are defined in zh/sync/api-conventions.md §11.2.

resource_kinds.description: Directory-service resource classes indexed by ak.find.directory.read.describe.v1. Required when service_kind=directory_service.

private_contact_discovery.description: Complete machine-readable configuration for ak.private_contact_discovery.v1. It is required exactly when the expanded supported_operation_bundles union contains (ak.find.directory.read.private_contact_discovery.v1,http_json); clients MUST fail closed if any field is absent or unsupported. Only the profile identity and the deployment-dynamic parameters (public key, key epoch, batch cardinality, handoff shape, precomputed phase buckets, completion TTL, quota and delay parameters) are carried; the parameters fixed by the profile identity are never echoed.

profile.description: Profile identity. It fixes RFC 9497 modeVOPRF (0x01), the ristretto255-SHA512 ciphersuite, the 16-byte derived prefix length, the single batched DLEQ proof shape, the [4096, 16384, 65536, 262144] response bucket set and the uniform anti-enumeration delay distribution; any change to one of these fixed parameters MUST be published as a new profile identity instead of a new describe field (zh/discovery/discovery-directory.md section 6.1).

public_key.description: Canonical unpadded base64url encoding of the active 32-byte ristretto255 VOPRF public key. Decoders additionally validate the group encoding and reject the identity element.

key_epoch.description: Epoch accepted for new blind requests. A batch admitted under an older epoch remains bound to its pinned key and cached outcome until its advertised completion TTL expires.

batch_item_count.description: Exact cardinality required for blinded_elements, evaluated_elements, derived_prefixes, hit_bitmap and, when enabled, handoff_stubs. Clients create indistinguishable dummy elements before sending the blind request.

handoff_stubs_mode.description: Shape is fixed for the advertised key epoch. always means handoff_stubs is present at every match position with dummy entries where necessary; never means the field is absent for every match outcome.

blind_response_bucket_bytes.description: Precomputed smallest bucket of the profile-fixed [4096, 16384, 65536, 262144] set that holds the largest RFC 8785 JCS body among the maximal legal blind success outcome and every allowed blind-phase Class B error projection for this configuration.

match_response_bucket_bytes.description: Precomputed smallest bucket of the profile-fixed [4096, 16384, 65536, 262144] set that holds the largest RFC 8785 JCS body among the maximal legal match success outcome and every allowed match-phase Class B error projection for this batch_item_count and handoff_stubs_mode.

batch_completion_ttl_seconds.description: Exact acceptance interval measured from successful blind admission. The provider retains the pinned key epoch, request bindings and cached outcomes throughout this interval; at or after admission_time + this value it rejects the batch as psi_batch_unavailable.

anti_enumeration_delay.description: Origin-side delay parameters shared by success and Class B paths for the same phase, sampled only after authentication and syntax validation. The distribution is fixed by the profile identity to minimum_ms + UniformInteger(0..jitter_ms).

restricted_query_proof.description: Whether the directory requires holder-approved proof for restricted or privacy-sensitive query classes.

accept_policy_kind.description: Directory resource acceptance policy advertised by ak.find.directory.read.describe.v1.

accept_policy_ref.description: Optional human-readable or governance reference describing how a resource obtains directory acceptance.

default_ttl_seconds.description: Default directory entry TTL in seconds.

max_ttl_seconds.description: Maximum accepted directory entry TTL in seconds.

revalidation_grace_seconds.description: Grace period for refreshing indexed resources after TTL expiry.

accepted_resource_kinds.description: Subset of resource kinds accepted by this directory instance.

accepted_did_methods.description: Principal/governance DID methods accepted by this directory instance.

takedown_contact.description: Operator takedown notification or appeal contact, expressed as a DID or URL.

rate_limits.description: Readable per-DID, per-organization or per-IP directory quota limits.

verified_profiles.description: Profiles for which a Conformance Verifier run (conformance-suite.md §6.2) has produced a passing verification artifact. Each entry MUST identify the verification run, artifact hash, artifact retrieval reference, verifier DID, verifier signature, and verification timestamp. When the service is in `development_mode=true` this array MUST be empty. Each profile_id MUST occur in supported_profiles and be unique within verified_profiles; consumers MUST verify this relationship and applicable artifact evidence before displaying a verified badge. Evidence alone MUST NOT activate a profile.

artifact_ref.description: URI or transparency-log reference from which the verification artifact can be fetched.

verifier_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the Conformance Verifier that signed the artifact statement. The artifact's DID URL signing key is verified separately and its canonical bare did MUST project through the registered adapter to this value.

signature.description: Signature over profile_id, verification_run_id, artifact_digest, artifact_ref, verifier and timestamp.

interop_surfaces.description: Surfaces this service exposes outside its claimed Arkret v1 conformance: bridged third-party protocols and delegated resolver postures. A service MUST NOT declare its own product-private route root here — a private API is neither a bridged foreign protocol nor a delegation, and declaring one would grant it a conformance-adjacent standing it does not have. The object is closed so such a declaration cannot be smuggled in through extension keys.

kind.description: matrix_passthrough / mimi_passthrough: bridged foreign protocol surface. delegated_resolver: a DID document / key-log surface served on behalf of a canonical authority this service does not claim to be (conformance-profiles.md §9). external_interop: any other non-Arkret interop surface. This list is exhaustive; product-private APIs have no member here.

development_mode.description: Mirror of the service's development_mode flag. When true, `verified_profiles` MUST be empty.

supported_operation_bundles.description: Canonical-sorted registered bundle ids this role endpoint fully implements. The local registry expands each id to exact (operation_id,binding_kind) pairs; unknown ids never grant availability.

transport_bindings.description: Transport endpoints in descending server preference. Operation coverage is not repeated here and comes only from supported_operation_bundles.

invite_addressing.description: Registered invite-addressing negotiation. Required when ak.feature.invite_addressing.v1 is advertised.

allOf.$comment: Calendar support or attached verification evidence requires executable TZDB releases. Verified entries MUST additionally be a subset of supported_profiles (semantic validation).

cidr.description: IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR string. Parsability and address-family semantics are enforced by the egress policy evaluator.

origin.description: Absolute origin of the client-visible Account Authority.

gate_account_base_url.description: Absolute base URL from which all client-visible /_arkret/gate/account/* endpoints MUST be derived.

kind.description: Every advertised interactive authentication method terminates in the AccountHandoff exchange. For OIDC, authentication-handoffs is the unique authorization-code consumer; SessionGrant issue never consumes the code.

transport_binding_websocket.description: WebSocket transport descriptor. kind=websocket fixes the required binding profile ak.profile.binding.websocket.v1, the arkret.v1 subprotocol and the challenge_dpop_session_v1 authentication through binding-kind-registry and the profile itself; the descriptor carries only the connection coordinates and transport limits.
